title: Scientists Put a Mirror in a Manta Ray Tank. It Wouldn't Leave

scenes.text: Scientists put a mirror in a manta ray tank. The rays wouldn't leave it.
Giant mantas swam back and forth in front of it, rolling and unrolling their head fins about ten times more often than normal.
They blew bubbles at the glass. And the white-spot display they flash at strangers never appeared.
Manta rays have the largest brain of any fish, so researchers tried the test on them.
The researcher says it leaves room for self-awareness, but doesn't prove it. Only a few animals, like apes and dolphins, clearly pass.

subject: manta ray
description:
Scientists put a mirror in a manta ray tank, and the rays wouldn't leave it.
They blew bubbles and rolled their head fins, and treated the reflection like no stranger.
Could a fish know it's looking at itself?
first_comment: Do you think a fish can know it's looking at itself? Or is it just curious?
